name: Business model
purpose: How does the firm create, deliver and capture value?

parts.label: Value creation
points: What is offered to which customer segment – needs, solution

parts.label: Value configuration
points: How the value chain is organized to deliver it

parts.label: Value capture
points: Why the model generates a margin – revenue and cost sources

parts.label: Created vs captured (Ryall 2013)
points: A firm can create much value but keep little
Capture depends on credible alternatives of customers, suppliers, partners

example: Airbnb: value for guests and hosts · multi-sided platform · commissions for Airbnb, payments for hosts.

name: Generic strategies

parts.label: 3. Focused cost leadership
points: Low cost, narrow market (local restaurant, fruit market)

parts.label: Axis 1: cost vs value
points: Cost advantage: structurally lower costs → lower prices or higher margins

parts.label: Axis 2: broad vs narrow scope
points: Market size by age, wealth, geography …

apply: Classify the firm on both axes with evidence
Check that value chain and structure fit the choice

name: Cost leadership – sources & structure
purpose: Where do structurally lower costs come from?

parts.label: Sources of lower costs
points: Economies of scale (until diseconomies, U-shaped LRAC)
Economies of learning – experience curve (capital & labour productivity)

parts.label: Challenges
points: Sustaining low costs over time and places
Human rights – labour is not a resource like capital

name: Differentiation – sources, structure & risks
purpose: How does a firm justify higher prices?

parts.label: Typical structure
points: Marketing & product R&D as main functions

parts.label: Risks
points: Too different: no attention or no value

example: Juicero: $120m VC, $400–700 press – perceived value without substantial added value.

name: Stuck in the middle
purpose: What happens without a clear choice between cost and value?

parts.label: Definition
points: Unclear position between cost leadership and differentiation
AND bad performance as a result

parts.label: Exceptions
points: Innovative offer combining both (blue ocean) – usually temporary

parts.label: Value logic
points: Cost advantage, value advantage, or dual advantage

example: JCPenney: could not beat Walmart on cost nor Macy's on value → near bankruptcy 2020.

name: Three ways to play a gold rush
purpose: Where in a booming value chain should a firm position itself?

parts.label: Dig for gold
points: Build and sell the best model (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind)

parts.label: Make jewellery
points: Own the complements (Meta, Chrome, Android, Workspace)
Want the gold cheap and abundant

example: Google tries all three and faces cannibalization of ad-funded search; gen-AI queries have real marginal costs (caps, tiers, routing, ads).
